summary.text: CA9 is the candidate with the most complete convergence. It is strongly up in tumour RNA (log2FC [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.31]) and protein (log2FC [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.27]), replicates in TCGA-KIRC and survives purity extrapolation. In single-cell data the RCC cells carry almost all of its tumour transcripts [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976]. It is a membrane protein with girentuximab in late-stage development, and the literature supports CA9 imaging. Two caveats limit it: it is not prognostic in TCGA, and the GTEx vital-organ proteome flags stomach expression, which matters for a conjugate or radioligand. It is best read as a surface target and diagnostic or imaging biomarker, not a dependency.

Two other surface antigens with clinical antibodies converge across omics, literature and tractability. CD70 is up at protein and in TCGA, and its low vital-organ protein specificity is favourable for safety. However, deconvolution attributes most of its bulk tumour transcripts to immune cells, and the two single-cell datasets disagree on its source cell, so how much CD70 tumour cells carry is unresolved. ENPP3 is an apical membrane enzyme with protein gain, TCGA replication and an ADC already tested clinically. The HIF-2 alpha axis anchors the biology: VHL is the founding driver, and EPAS1 is the only highly ranked gene with a ccRCC-selective DepMap signal and an approved drug (belzutifan). Its transcripts sit mostly in endothelium and fibroblasts, so its bulk RNA does not reflect tumour-cell pathway activity.

Purely data-driven candidates complete the target list. SCARB1 (the HDL receptor) leads the target profile, is tumour-intrinsic, has Open Targets genetic support and its protein gain replicates in the confirmatory DIA cohort. But it has no ccRCC literature in the corpus, adrenal enrichment, and patchy expression across tumour cells. NNMT is up at RNA and protein, its protein gain replicates in the confirmatory cohort, it is assigned to tumour cells in both single-cell datasets, and high expression is associated with worse survival in TCGA, so it is both target and prognostic biomarker. SLC16A3 (MCT4) fits the glycolytic HIF programme but its source cell is not replicated across datasets. On the biomarker side, the strongest calls are loss-of-expression genes: PSAT1 and PCK1 (protein loss replicated in the confirmatory cohort and lower in the ccB subtype), and ALDOB (low expression associated with worse survival). UMOD, too, marks the loss of tubule identity. COXFA4L2 is strongly up and highly convergent, but no selective drug or dependency supports it as a target.

Unexplored candidates identified and prioritised for experimental validation. The convergence ranking rewards literature and existing drugs, so little-studied genes come from the discovery screen. In the tumour-cell track, COL23A1 leads. RCC cells make most of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881], it replicates in TCGA and stays high when extrapolated to a pure tumour, it has a UniProt membrane annotation, and vital-organ expression is low. What is missing is confirmed surface exposure (SURFY and CSPA do not confirm it), staining in normal tissues, any dependency or survival signal, and a reliable structure. Surface proteomics and immunohistochemistry on tumour and normal kidney would test it as an antibody antigen. RAB42 is second: it is mostly made by RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627], replicates in TCGA and is purity-robust. But it is an intracellular small GTPase, so it is not antibody-accessible, and it has no functional or dependency data. Knockdown in ccRCC models with intact HIF-2 signalling would be the first test. Stroma (OLFML2A, JAG2) and immune (GAL3ST4, LILRB4, MILR1) candidates also emerge. Several immune ones lose their change on purity extrapolation, so they report infiltration rather than tumour-cell biology. Here novel means few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, and none of these genes is shown to be a selective dependency.

Across the candidates, the evidence is expression-based. Apart from EPAS1, no highly ranked gene shows a ccRCC-selective DepMap dependency. Treatment-trial associations (CA9 and CD70 with longer benefit on sunitinib or atezolizumab plus bevacizumab) do not survive multiple-testing correction, and no gene separates the main trial arms. These are leads for prospective testing, not predictive biomarkers.

omics.text: Tumour-versus-normal CPTAC data separate two groups. The first is HIF-driven genes gained in tumour: CA9, CD70, NNMT, SCARB1, SLC16A3, ENPP3 and the lipid-droplet regulator HILPDA. The second is tubule-identity genes lost in tumour: UMOD, ALDOB and PSAT1. The gained group is consistent across RNA and protein. NNMT, for example, is up at protein (log2FC [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.71]) and SLC16A3 at protein (log2FC [gene=SLC16A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.28]) with a positive copy-number cis effect. HILPDA is strongly up in RNA (log2FC [gene=HILPDA; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=5.12]) but has no tractability and reads as a pathway marker. The lost group is dominated by UMOD (RNA log2FC [gene=UMOD; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=-10.31]) and ALDOB (RNA log2FC [gene=ALDOB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=-7.03]). These reflect cell-of-origin loss and are diagnostic markers, not targets.

VHL explains the gained HIF-target group. Chromosome-arm loss affects most CPTAC tumours [gene=VHL; type=omics_cnv; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; loss_freq=79.1%], and somatic mutation affects about half of the combined cohort [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=48.3%]. As a loss-of-function tumour suppressor it cannot be inhibited directly. Its relevance is as the upstream cause of HIF-2 alpha activation.

literature.text: The literature supports CA9 and CD70 most directly, as tumour-enriched antigens with imaging or antibody development. A CA9 PET study shows proof-of-concept discrimination of ccRCC but awaits prospective validation. For CD70, single-domain antibody radiotracers have been developed and expression is linked to hypoxia signalling. For COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2), there is HIF-dependent overexpression and a proposed ferroptosis-suppressing mechanism, but the support is preclinical. For NNMT, the corpus reports up-regulation and worse survival with high expression, which agrees with the TCGA data, and selective chemical inhibitors exist outside ccRCC.

For the down-regulated genes, ALDOB and SLC22A8 are described in single bioinformatic or immunohistochemistry studies as prognostic loss-of-expression markers, which is consistent with the data. The MT1G literature contradicts itself: it is lower in tumour than normal, yet within tumours higher levels track with worse outcome. SCARB1 and PIGR are supported by data but are silent in the literature corpus. Absence from this limited corpus is not absence from the field.

external.text: Open Targets and UniProt confirm that the leading up-regulated antigens are tractable membrane proteins with clinical history. CA9 has girentuximab and sulfonamide-class compounds. CD70 has cusatuzumab and vorsetuzumab mafodotin. ENPP3 has the ADC AGS-16C3F. EPAS1 is the established small-molecule target, with belzutifan approved. Except for EPAS1, DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency for any of these. They are antigen cases (antibody, conjugate or imaging), not intrinsic vulnerabilities.

EPAS1 carries the strongest genetic and functional external support among the targets. Its Open Targets association score is [gene=EPAS1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4871]. ccRCC lines are more dependent on it than other lines [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3], although the adjusted q-value is borderline. Its convergence rank is modest because RNA differential expression is weak, which shows that the convergence score under-weights pathway targets whose activity is post-translational.

cells.text: The single-cell data separate tumour-intrinsic candidates from microenvironment ones. CA9 and MET are made by RCC cells. MET holds most of its tumour transcripts in RCC cells [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935]. CA9 is essentially absent from proximal tubule cells (tumour-vs-PT log2FC [gene=CA9; type=sc_tumor_vs_pt; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; log2fc=7.739]). NNMT is assigned to tumour cells in both single-cell datasets. Several bulk candidates are not tumour-intrinsic. KDR is endothelial [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951]. CD74 is mainly macrophage and dendritic [gene=CD74; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.436], and CXCR4 is lymphocytic. EPAS1 transcripts sit in endothelium and fibroblasts, and the RCC share is small [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.051].

CD70 and SLC16A3 have unresolved cell sources. Both are dominated by T and NK cells in Li 2022 but by tumour cells in Zhang 2021. For CD70, the CPTAC deconvolution adds that most bulk transcripts are immune-attributed, even though the bulk change survives purity extrapolation. Tumour-cell specificity for these two is therefore partial, and the claim needs protein-level confirmation in tumour cells.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, composition-corrected attribution explains CA9 high-expression spots almost entirely by RCC spots. Their immediate neighbours are enriched in RCC and, more weakly, in macrophages, both significant after correction. This is consistent with tumour-cell clusters as the source, not stroma.

structure.text: Structural context is a descriptive heuristic on predicted monomers, not evidence of a degron or degrader. The AlphaFold CA9 model has a detected cavity of [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; volume_a3=126.8] cubic angstrom with a modest structural-context score, and detected cavities recover part of the experimental ligand-contact residues. CA9 already has antibody and sulfonamide-class clinical history. The discovery candidate COL23A1 has a low-confidence model (mean pLDDT [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91]) with only a tiny shallow cavity. Structure-based tractability is therefore unsupported for it, which does not exclude antibody targeting. No curated experimental degron or ternary-complex reference applies to these candidates.

discovery.text: COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, leads the tumour-cell track of the discovery screen. RCC cells, not stroma, make most of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. The tumour gain replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; tcga_log2fc=5.829], and it holds when extrapolated to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88]. It has few ccRCC papers, no clinical drug and low vital-organ expression. Missing are confirmed surface exposure, an adverse survival association and any DepMap dependency. It is a data-ranked hypothesis for surface-proteomic and immunohistochemical follow-up.

RAB42, a small Rab GTPase, is the second tumour-track candidate. It is mainly expressed by RCC cells [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627], is up in TCGA and is purity-robust, and it has very few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug. It is intracellular, so antibodies and conjugates cannot reach it. It shows no adverse survival and no dependency, so it needs functional work, such as knockdown in ccRCC models, before it can be called a target.

The stroma track offers OLFML2A, a secreted fibroblast gene (fibroblast share [gene=OLFML2A; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.647]) with some colon expression. It also offers JAG2, an endothelial Notch ligand (endothelial share [gene=JAG2; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=stroma; source_share=0.487]) that is antibody-tractable but shows a modest tumour-versus-normal change and heart expression. Both replicate in TCGA, are purity-robust and lack survival or dependency signals.

The immune track is where most of the novel pool lives, and purity extrapolation is decisive there. MILR1 and LILRB4 are macrophage genes whose tumour-versus-normal change nearly vanishes in a pure tumour: MILR1 [gene=MILR1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414] and LILRB4 [gene=LILRB4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.508]. They report macrophage infiltration rather than a tumour-cell change. GAL3ST4 is almost entirely macrophage-derived [gene=GAL3ST4; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=immune; source_share=0.972] and purity-robust, and it is associated with adverse survival. But it is an intracellular enzyme with no dependency data.

validation.text: Independent layers strengthen several candidates. CA9 and CD70 replicate strongly in TCGA-KIRC: CA9 [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.71] and CD70 [gene=CD70; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=7.09]. ENPP3 also replicates [gene=ENPP3; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.56]. In the confirmatory CPTAC DIA cohort, protein changes replicate in the discovery direction for SCARB1 [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334], NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776], PSAT1 [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946] and PCK1. CD70 was not testable there because coverage was too sparse, which is a gap, not a failed replication.

Prognosis and dependency are thinner. High NNMT and PSAT1 expression, and low ALDOB expression, are associated with worse TCGA survival. CA9, CD70 and SCARB1 are not prognostic. VHL is the only recurrent somatic driver among the candidates. Apart from EPAS1, DepMap shows no ccRCC-selective dependency for any candidate, partly because two-dimensional culture misses HIF-2 biology. The purity check strengthens CA9, CD70, NNMT and the tumour-track discovery genes, whose changes survive extrapolation to a pure tumour. It weakens immune-track genes such as MILR1 and LILRB4, whose changes disappear.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the evidence streams, CA9 and COXFA4L2 are the only genes that stay in the overall top ten in most draws, and both stay in the top 25 whichever stream is removed. In the target profile, SCARB1 and CA9 are the most stable, followed by SLC16A3, CD70 and NNMT, with narrow rank intervals. SLC16A3 and HK2 fall out of the target top 25 if the tumour-up omics stream is removed. SCARB1 and PIGR depend on the genetics stream for their overall position, and NNMT on the literature stream.

In the biomarker profile, PSAT1 is the most robust call, and PCK1 is also stable. Lower biomarker-profile positions, such as SLPI, VWF, DUSP9 and L1CAM, swing widely with the weights and should be treated as weight-dependent. CA9 and ALDOB keep a high biomarker position only with several streams together.

treatment.text: In the treatment-response trials, associations are leads only. Higher CD70 expression is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=-0.383]. CA9 is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336]. Neither association survives adjustment of the p-value, and higher PSAT1 tracks with earlier progression in every arm, again without adjusted significance. No gene separates the combination arm from sunitinib, or nivolumab from everolimus, so none is a treatment-selection marker on this evidence.

subtypes.text: CA9 is a PBRM1 subgroup candidate. It is higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours in CPTAC RNA, CPTAC protein and TCGA RNA (TCGA mutant-minus-wildtype [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148]), but the protein difference is small and CA9 is lower in ccB. PSAT1 is higher in BAP1-mutant tumours at TCGA RNA level [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711] and higher in ccB, so it is a poor-prognosis subtype marker, not a subgroup target. PCK1 is much lower in ccB at RNA level, and SCARB1 is a pan-tumour candidate without a subgroup flag. Subtype differences in immune genes may reflect infiltration rather than tumour-cell biology.

adc.text: For an antibody-drug conjugate or radioligand, CD70 has a high suitability score [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746], consistent with its role as a known conjugate target and acting as a positive control, though no staining data were available. CA9 is a known target, but vital-organ protein specificity is high in stomach [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19], which is a safety concern. SCARB1 is surface-observed but adrenal-enriched, and only a small share of tumour cells express it in the weakest donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%]. SLC16A3 is the most homogeneous [gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=43.7%], but as a multi-pass transporter with few extracellular residues, antibody access is doubtful. A high score does not show that a conjugate would work.

immune.text: CPTAC deconvolution attributes most CD70 tumour transcripts to immune cells [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654]. CD70 correlates positively with CD8 and regulatory T cells, so its bulk signal rises in inflamed (hot) tumours. SCARB1 draws about half of its transcripts from immune cells but correlates negatively with the immune score and CD8 T cells, so it is higher in cold tumours and is not a checkpoint-like gene. The single-cell data confirm CD74 and CXCR4 as immune-cell controls, and they show the immune-track discovery genes as macrophage-abundance readouts.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge most clearly on CA9 and CD70: tumour-up, replicated, membrane-located and clinically tractable. ENPP3 and EPAS1 complete the set of established targets, with EPAS1 supported by genetics, dependency and an approved drug rather than by expression. They disagree in three places. COXFA4L2 has strong omics and literature but no selective drug or dependency. SCARB1 is data-strong but literature-silent. And the cell-type layers show that part of the bulk signal for CD70, SLC16A3 and EPAS1 comes from non-tumour cells. Down-regulated tubule genes (ALDOB, UMOD, PSAT1, PCK1) are biomarkers of lost tubule identity and prognosis, not targets. HILPDA and VHL describe the HIF mechanism rather than separate drug opportunities.

targets.rationale: Most complete convergence: tumour-up at RNA and protein, made by tumour cells, replicated in TCGA, purity-robust and robust in both profiles. A membrane antigen with girentuximab and imaging literature. Stomach expression in vital organs and lack of prognostic value are the main caveats.

Tumour-up, replicated, purity-robust membrane ligand with clinical antibodies and a high conjugate suitability score. Its immune-cell share and the unreplicated single-cell source temper tumour-cell specificity, and it is untested in the confirmatory cohort.

Placed above its convergence rank: it is the only candidate with a ccRCC-selective DepMap signal, it has strong Open Targets association, and belzutifan is approved. Expression-based scoring under-weights it, and its transcripts are mostly stromal.
Apical membrane enzyme with protein gain, TCGA replication, no vital-organ enrichment and an ADC already tested clinically. Ranked lower overall but a coherent antigen case. No dependency.

Up at RNA and protein, assigned to tumour cells in two single-cell datasets, protein replicated in the confirmatory cohort, and adverse TCGA survival concordant with the literature. Selective inhibitors exist outside ccRCC, but there is no dependency or clinical drug.

Top and most robust target-profile gene: tumour-intrinsic, with genetic association and protein replicated in the confirmatory cohort. Ranked below the established antigens because it is literature-silent, adrenal-enriched, has heterogeneous tumour expression and has no clinical drug.

MCT4 lactate exporter in the HIF glycolytic programme, up across layers and with homogeneous expression. The cell source is not replicated between single-cell datasets, antibody access is poor, and there is no dependency.
Most robust biomarker-profile gene. Protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort, it is associated with adverse TCGA survival, and it is higher in ccB. A prognostic marker, not a target.
Strong tumour loss replicated in TCGA, with low expression associated with worse survival, consistent with the literature. A loss-of-expression diagnostic and prognostic marker.
Stable in the biomarker profile, with protein loss and phosphosites replicated in the confirmatory cohort, and lower in ccB at RNA level. Lost in tumour, so a biomarker only.
Second in overall convergence and robust, with strong RNA and protein gain and rich preclinical literature. Classed as a biomarker because no selective drug or dependency supports targeting.
Among the most strongly lost genes, marking the loss of tubule identity. A diagnostic tissue marker, and its position partly depends on the literature stream.

Exploratory: top tumour-track discovery gene, made by RCC cells, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, with low vital-organ expression. Main limitation: surface exposure is unconfirmed and there is no survival or dependency signal.

Exploratory: second tumour-track discovery gene, RCC-cell-derived, TCGA-replicated and purity-robust. Main limitation: intracellular, so not antibody-accessible, with no functional or dependency evidence.

limitations.text: Evidence is predominantly expression-based. DepMap and PRISM use two-dimensional cell lines that miss HIF-2 and microenvironment biology, so the lack of selective dependency does not exclude a target.
Treatment-response associations come from small trial arms and none survives multiple-testing correction. They are leads, not predictive biomarkers.
The literature corpus is a limited set of ccRCC abstracts. Literature silence (SCARB1, PIGR, discovery genes) means absence from the corpus, and the convergence score favours well-studied genes.
Single-cell attribution disagrees between Li 2022 and Zhang 2021 for CD70 and SLC16A3. Zhang 2021 has few paired donors, and purity extrapolation is model-based.
The GTEx proteome lacks kidney and has limited detection, so the absence of vital-organ signal is not proof of safety. Conjugate suitability scores do not show that a conjugate would work.
Not every candidate was profiled in every layer. HK2, ENPP3 and EPAS1 were not checked in the confirmatory cohort in this run, and survival models are univariate.
Structural-context scores are monomer cavity heuristics. They do not identify degrons or predict degradation, and no curated ternary-complex reference applies to these candidates.
Passing the automatic checks is not complete scientific validation. Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses prioritised for experimental validation, not discoveries.
